The Bank of Japan, acting as the agent for the Minister of Finance, Japan, and the RBI signed the third Amendment and Restatement Agreement of the BSA. The BSA is a two-way arrangement where both authorities can swap their local currencies in exchange for the US Dollar. The size of the BSA remains unchanged, that is, up to $75 billion. Renewal of the Bilateral Swap Arrangement (BSA) between Japan and India effective from February 28, 2026 Japan and India believe that the BSA, which aims to strengthen and complement other financial safety nets, will further deepen financial cooperation between the two countries and contribute to regional and global financial stability.

# Page 6^page=6
Understanding Acquisition Finance refers to a loan or financial assistance given to an eligible borrower for: Purchasing equity shares or Compulsorily Convertible Debentures (CCDs) In a target company With the objective of acquiring control over the target company Acquisition finance may be extended by a Commercial bank to an Indian non- financial company for acquiring equity stakes in domestic or foreign companies as strategic investments, i.e. those investments which are driven by the core objective of creating long-term value for the acquirer through potential synergies, rather than mere financial restructuring for short-term gains.

# Page 7^page=7
Eligible Entities Acquisition finance can be extended to: the acquiring company, being a non-financial company, directly; or an existing non-financial subsidiary of the acquiring company; or a step-down special purpose vehicle (SPV) set up by the acquiring company specifically for the purpose.

# Page 8^page=8
Acquisition finance shall be subject to the following conditions: - Financial criteria The acquiring company (or, where acquisition is through an SPV or subsidiary, the acquiring company controlling such SPV or subsidiary) shall meet the following financial criteria at the time of sanctioning the acquisition finance: Unlisted Entities and Listed Entities (on a recognized stock exchange in India): (a) Minimum net worth of ₹500 crore; and (b) Net profit after taxes reported in each of the previous three consecutive financial years. Additional Criteria for unlisted entities: (c) an investment grade rating (BBB- or above) from a credit rating agency. If there is no rating available for the acquiring company at the time of sanction, it shall have to be obtained prior to disbursement of acquisition finance.

# Page 9^page=9
Acquisition finance shall be subject to the following conditions: Related Party Restrictions: The acquiring company and the target company shall not be related parties, where "related party" means: Entities that have relationships such as: Holding–subsidiary relationship, Associate companies, a firm, in which a director, manager or his relative is a partner, Common directors, Key managerial personnel relationships Entities under common control, common management, or common promoter group, whether directly or indirectly. Control acquisition requirements: The acquisition shall result in the acquirer obtaining control of the target company through a single transaction, or a series of inter-connected transactions but completed within 12 months from the date of execution of the acquisition agreement. • Where the acquiring company already holds control over the target company, acquisition finance may be extended only for acquiring additional stake that crosses a substantial threshold of 26 per cent, 51 per cent, 75 per cent, 90 per cent of voting rights, each conferring materially enhanced governance or control rights under applicable law.

# Page 10^page=10
Financing Parameters Credit assessment shall be conducted on a consolidated basis, incorporating the financials of both the acquiring and target entities. Total bank financing shall not exceed 75% of the acquisition value, as independently assessed by the bank as under: Listed Company: Valuation as determined by one independent valuer (to be appointed by the bank) for valuing shares not frequently traded Unlisted company: Lower of the valuation determined by two independent valuers (to be appointed by the bank) for valuing shares not frequently traded If the target is a listed company, but its shares are not frequently traded, then: The acquisition value cannot be based simply on market price. Instead: •The bank must appoint one independent valuer •The valuer determines the fair value of shares

# Page 11^page=11
Financing Parameters The acquiring company must contribute the remaining amount from its own funds, such as internal accruals or fresh equity. A corporate guarantee from the acquiring company, or its parent or the group holding entity, shall be mandatory. Post-acquisition, Debt to Equity ratio at the acquiring company's consolidated balance sheet level shall not exceed 3:1 on a continuous basis.

# Page 12^page=12
Financing Parameters While the acquiring company, if listed, may utilize bridge finance to satisfy the minimum own funds requirement of 25%, acquisition finance in such cases shall be subject to the following conditions: Clear Repayment Plan There must be a clear source to repay the bridge loan, such as: Issuing new shares (equity issue) or Selling assets And this must happen within 12 months. If a bank provides the bridge loan, it must be secured with collateral. bridge finance should not result in dilution of security coverage for the acquisition finance "Bridge Finance" shall mean financing a borrower for an interim period, not exceeding one year, for a legitimate business purpose where the borrower has a firm plan and capability to repay such loans by raising financial resources.

# Page 13^page=13
Security Creation and Valuation Acquisition finance shall be secured by the acquired equity shares/CCDs of the target company. Other assets of the acquirer and/or target company, and promoter's personal guarantee may be taken as additional collateral as per the bank's policy. Acquisition finance undertaken by overseas branches of Indian banks as part of syndication arrangements, shall not be subject to the Directions given in this chapter provided that, the funding contribution of a bank under such a syndication arrangement for a particular deal shall not exceed 20% of total funding under the deal.

# Page 14^page=14
Summary

# Page 15^page=15
The above amendments shall come into force from April 1, 2026, or an earlier date when adopted by a bank in entirety.

Q1. Consider the following statements regarding the Bilateral Swap Arrangement (BSA) between India and Japan: I. The Bank of Japan acts as the primary principal in the agreement, while the Reserve Bank of India acts as the agent for the Government of India. II. The BSA allows both the RBI and the Japanese authorities to exchange their respective local currencies for US Dollars. III. Under the third Amendment and Restatement Agreement, the maximum swap limit was expanded to $100 billion to accommodate increasing trade volume. Which of the statements given above is/are CORRECT? A) Only II B) Only I and II C) Only I D) Only II and III E) I, II, and III MCQs for Practice

Q2. Regarding the RBI guidelines on Acquisition Finance (2025-26), consider the following statements: I. For an unlisted acquiring company to be eligible, it must have a minimum net worth of ₹500 crore, previous three consecutive years of net profit after taxes, and an investment-grade rating of at least BBB- before disbursement. II. Total bank financing for an acquisition is capped at 75% of the acquisition value, while the post-acquisition consolidated Debt-to-Equity ratio must not exceed 3:2 on a continuous basis. III. The acquisition shall result in the acquirer obtaining control of the target company through a single transaction, or a series of inter-connected transactions but completed within 6 months from the date of execution of the acquisition agreement. Which of the statements given above is/are INCORRECT? A) Only I and II B) Only II and III C) Only I and III D) I, II, and III E) Only I MCQs for Practice
